newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA CLOSE IN ON SECOND TEST WIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA CLOSE IN ON SECOND TEST WIN.

text.p: India were left needing a second monumental innings from their captain Sachin Tendulkar after South Africa took a tight grip of the second test at Newlands on Sunday.

Tendulkar, who made a brilliant 169 in India's first innings to ensure they avoided the follow-on, was undefeated on six at the close of the fourth day as India, set an unlikely 427 to win, struggled to 52 for three.
The Indian captain needs to produce the kind of innings with which England captain Mike Atherton saved a test in Johannesburg last season.
His task is to bat all day on Monday to avoid a second defeat or, more improbably, help India score a further 375 runs to level the three-test series after their 328-run defeat in Durban.
India were set 427 for victory from a minimum of 118 overs after South Africa again dominated the day's play, declaring their second innings on 256 for six three overs after tea.
In the 28 overs they faced, India were again quickly in trouble.
In the seventh over Allan Donald knocked back opener Nayan Mongia's off-stump and then Woorkeri Raman got a thin edge to Shaun Pollock and keeper Dave Richardson took a good, diving catch.
It became 44 for three when Rahul Dravid nibbled at left-arm spinner Paul Adams' chinaman and was also caught by Richardson.

After the early loss of nightwatchman Lance Klusener, South Africa recovered well with two excellent partnerships, both records for the home side against India, to reach 256 for six before they declared three overs after tea.

Andrew Hudson and Daryll Cullinan, who both made 55, put on 94 for the fourth wicket and then, after three wickets had gone in quick succession, Brian McMillan and Shaun Pollock added 101 in an unbroken seventh wicket stand.
Cullinan went to his second half-century of the match in just 71 balls while Hudson played the anchor role.

They fell within seven runs of each other shortly after lunch as they looked to force the pace. Cullinan was bowled by leg-spinner Anil Kumble and Hudson chopped a ball from Javagal Srinath on to his stumps.
When Hansie Cronje was snapped up by Dravid at short-leg off Kumble for 18, South Africa were 155 for six but McMillan, 59 not out, and Pollock, 40 not out, regained the initiative.
Their century partnership came in just 87 minutes with McMillan, who made an unbeaten 103 in the first innings, taking his aggregate for the series to 247 for once out.
